test_title: PYST 56: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held on 05 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation focusing on the underlined segment.

I know every detail of his accident because I __heard the facts directly__ from him.

options.text: Get something out of your system

solution: The correct answer is **'Straight from horse's mouth'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The most appropriate meaning of the idiom is **'Straight from horse's mouth'. **(सीधे स्रोत से जानकारी प्राप्त करना) • In the given sentence, "**heard the facts directly"** means** 'to know something directly from one's mouth'.** • Hence, the correct idiom is **'Straight from horse's mouth'.** • **Eg. -​** I heard the news about their engagement straight from the horse's mouth. Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 4'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • Option 1, '**Speak of the devil**' means **someone has been talking about has unexpectedly appeared**. (जिसको हम याद कर रहे होते हैं, और वह प्रकट हो जाता है I) • Option 2, '**Get something out of your system**' means **to do something that one has been wanting to do so that one no longer feel a strong desire to do it. **(किसी चीज़ को मन से निकाल देना I) • Option 3, '**Pour one’s heart out**' means** to speak very freely to someone about one's private and most deeply felt emotions. (**अपने दिल की बात कहना I) 36:Tf7b, The correct answer is **'Numismatics'.**
